title: Fully Funded PhD in International Relations at USIU-Africa Under the WATERSHED Project (2026): Complete Guide to Eligibility, Research Focus, Benefits, and Application Process
summary: The United States International University-Africa (USIU-Africa) , through its WATERSHED Research Project , has opened applications for a fully funded PhD in International Relations, offering an outstanding opportunity for aspiring researchers interested in climate adaptation, urban resilience, gender studies, and climate justice. Hosted by the Department of International Relations at USIU-Africa in Nairobi, Kenya , this doctoral opportunity is designed for highly motivated graduates who wish to contribute to groundbreaking research addressing climate change and flooding challenges affecting informal urban settlements. Funded by the Danida Fellowship Centre (DFC) , the WATERSHED Project seeks to bridge the gap between community-led climate adaptation initiatives and formal climate governance, producing research that informs policy while amplifying the voices of vulnerable communities. Application Deadline Deadline: 17 August 2026 Late or incomplete applications will not be considered , so interested applicants are encouraged to prepare and submit their applications well before the deadline. About USIU-Africa United States International University-Africa (USIU-Africa) is one of East Africa s leading private universities, recognized for delivering globally competitive education and research. The university s School of Humanities and Social Sciences promotes excellence in teaching, research, and innovation while preparing graduates to become critical thinkers and global citizens capable of addressing complex regional and international challenges. The fully funded doctoral opportunity is offered through the Department of International Relations, providing scholars with an environment that supports interdisciplinary research and international collaboration. About the WATERSHED Research Project The PhD position forms part of the WATERSHED Project , a research initiative funded by the Danida Fellowship Centre (DFC) . The project focuses on understanding how informal communities respond to increasing climate risks, particularly flooding, in Nairobi s rapidly growing urban settlements. Rather than examining climate adaptation only from the perspective of governments and institutions, WATERSHED investigates the everyday actions taken by community members and local activists who often play a critical role in building resilience despite receiving limited recognition. The project explores how grassroots initiatives can contribute to broader climate governance and policy development while addressing the challenges created by urbanization, environmental degradation, and changing development funding priorities. Read More Research Focus of the PhD Project The selected PhD researcher will develop a research project centered on: Flooding in Nairobi s informal settlements Community responses to climate change Gendered dimensions of climate adaptation Climate justice Informal governance Urban resilience Community-led adaptation strategies The research will specifically examine flooding and community and gender-related activities associated with climate adaptation measures in informal settlements across Nairobi. Areas of Study Applicants may draw on perspectives from several disciplines, including: International Relations Political Science Sociology Gender Studies Human Geography Anthropology Development Studies Other related Social Science fields This interdisciplinary approach allows the researcher to investigate climate adaptation from political, social, economic, environmental, and cultural perspectives. Why This Research Matters Climate change continues to increase the frequency and severity of flooding across many urban areas in Africa. Informal settlements are often among the hardest-hit communities because they typically experience: Poor drainage infrastructure High population density Limited public services Inadequate housing Greater exposure to environmental hazards Despite these challenges, local communities The WATERSHED Project seeks to document and understand these efforts while identifying how community knowledge can inform future climate policies and decision-making. Key Research Themes The project examines several interconnected themes, including: 1. Climate Adaptation Understanding how communities adapt to recurring flooding and changing environmental conditions. 2. Climate Justice Investigating whether vulnerable populations receive equitable support and representation in climate decision-making. 3. Community Activism Exploring how local residents organize themselves to improve resilience and advocate for better environmental management. 4. Urban Governance Assessing the relationship between government policies, planning decisions, and climate vulnerability. 5. Gender and Climate Change Examining how flooding and climate adaptation affect different groups within communities, particularly women and other marginalized populations. Study Locations The research will focus on three densely populated informal settlements located along Nairobi s river systems: Mathare Pumwani Korogocho These communities provide important case studies for understanding climate vulnerability and local adaptation practices within rapidly expanding urban environments. Project Objectives The WATERSHED Project aims to: Understand local perceptions of climate vulnerability. Examine community-led climate adaptation initiatives. Investigate climate justice actions within informal settlements. Explore the relationship between grassroots adaptation and formal climate governance. Generate evidence that can improve future climate policies. Strengthen knowledge on urban resilience in rapidly growing African cities. Who Should Apply? The university encourages applications from qualified and motivated candidates with a passion for research and social impact. Applicants should possess a graduate degree in one of the following disciplines: Political Science International Relations Sociology Gender Studies Human Geography Anthropology Development Studies Other relevant Social Science disciplines Candidates with research interests aligned with climate change, governance, urban development, community engagement, or environmental justice are particularly encouraged to apply. Funding This is a fully funded PhD position under the WATERSHED Research Project, supported by the Danida Fellowship Centre (DFC) . The announcement confirms that the PhD position is fully funded. However, it does not specify the exact financial package or benefits. Applicants are encouraged to consult the official call document or contact the project team for additional funding details. Why You Should Apply This opportunity offers numerous advantages, including: Full funding for doctoral studies. Opportunity to conduct impactful research on climate change and urban resilience. Collaboration with experienced researchers and academic experts. Participation in an internationally funded research initiative. Contribution to evidence-based climate governance and policy development. Research experience addressing real-world environmental and social challenges. How to Apply Interested applicants should submit their application in accordance with the official PhD call issued by USIU-Africa. Applicants should ensure that: They meet the eligibility requirements. Their research interests align with the WATERSHED Project. All required application materials are submitted before the deadline. Their application is complete, as incomplete submissions will not be considered. APPLY NOW Contact Information For inquiries regarding the PhD position, applicants may contact: Email 1: nwamai@usiu.ac.ke Email 2: watershedscholar@usiu.ac.ke Applicants are also encouraged to consult the official Call for PhD Researcher – WATERSHED Project for detailed application requirements and submission instructions. Conclusion The Fully Funded PhD in International Relations under the WATERSHED Project at USIU-Africa presents an exceptional opportunity for aspiring researchers who want to contribute to meaningful solutions for climate adaptation, climate justice, and urban resilience in Africa. By examining community-led responses to flooding in Nairobi s informal settlements, the successful candidate will be part of an internationally funded research initiative with the potential to influence policy, strengthen climate governance, and improve the lives of vulnerable urban communities. Prospective applicants with backgrounds in the social sciences and a commitment to impactful research should take advantage of this opportunity and ensure they submit a complete application before 17 August 2026 . title: Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers 2026: Apply for the Two-Day Green Entrepreneurship Training Programme in Accra, Ghana
summary: The Green Africa Youth Organization is inviting applications for the Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers 2026 , a two-day capacity-building programme designed to equip young entrepreneurs and waste workers with the practical knowledge, business skills, and professional networks needed to establish, formalize, and scale sustainable businesses. Formerly known as the Youth Ecopreneurs Summit and Training , the programme has evolved into a comprehensive training initiative that supports youth-led green enterprises while promoting environmental sustainability and economic empowerment. The training is specifically designed for residents of Accra, Ghana , and provides participants with expert-led sessions, practical workshops, mentorship opportunities, and networking experiences that can help transform innovative green business ideas into successful enterprises. Application Deadline: 14 August 2026 About the Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers 2026 The Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers is a strategic initiative focused on empowering young entrepreneurs working within the green economy. As environmental sustainability continues to become an important part of economic development, there is an increasing demand for businesses that provide innovative and environmentally responsible solutions. This programme seeks to bridge the knowledge gap by equipping participants with the entrepreneurial, financial, and marketing skills required to build sustainable businesses that contribute positively to both society and the environment. Whether participants already operate a small green business or are still developing an innovative business concept, the training provides practical guidance to help them move to the next stage of business development. The programme combines classroom learning with practical workshops, allowing participants to gain real-world insights into running successful green enterprises. Objectives of the Programme The Green Business Training aims to prepare participants for long-term success by helping them: Understand the fundamentals of business structuring and business management. Improve financial literacy and develop sound financial management practices. Learn about available investment opportunities for green businesses. Build effective branding and digital marketing strategies. Connect with experienced entrepreneurs and professionals within the green economy. Learn practical approaches to attracting funding and investment. Develop strategies for formalizing and scaling environmentally sustainable businesses. What Participants Will Learn The training covers a broad range of topics that are essential for launching, managing, and expanding a successful green enterprise. 1. Business Structuring and Business Management Participants will receive practical guidance on how to establish and organize their businesses for sustainable growth. Topics include: Business planning Business registration and formalization Organizational management Operational planning Strategic decision-making Building sustainable business models Understanding these areas will help participants build businesses capable of long-term success. 2. Financial Literacy and Investment Readiness Financial management is one of the most important components of business success. Participants will gain knowledge on: Financial planning Budgeting Managing business finances Preparing businesses for investors Understanding investment opportunities Improving financial sustainability The training will also introduce participants to methods for making their businesses more attractive to potential investors and funding organizations. 3. Access to Funding and Grant Writing One of the major challenges facing young entrepreneurs is securing financial support. Participants will explore: Available funding opportunities Grant application strategies Proposal writing techniques Preparing funding applications Understanding donor expectations These sessions are intended to improve participants ability to successfully compete for grants and other sources of business financing. 4. Digital Marketing and Branding In today s digital economy, having a strong online presence is essential. Participants will learn how to: Develop a recognizable business brand Market products and services online Improve customer engagement Increase business visibility Build effective digital marketing campaigns The programme will provide practical strategies that entrepreneurs can apply immediately to grow their businesses. 5. Networking and Mentorship A successful business often depends on having access to experienced professionals and valuable business networks. Participants will have opportunities to: Meet fellow young entrepreneurs. Connect with industry experts. Interact with successful green business leaders. Build partnerships within the green entrepreneurship ecosystem. Learn from experienced mentors. These networking opportunities can lead to future collaborations, partnerships, and business growth. Benefits of Participating Successful participants will enjoy several valuable benefits, including: Comprehensive training in green business development. Practical knowledge in business operations and management. Improved financial planning and investment readiness. Training on grant writing and funding opportunities. Digital marketing and branding skills. Opportunities to network with entrepreneurs and industry experts. Professional mentorship. A certificate upon successful completion of the programme. Who Can Apply? Applicants must satisfy all of the following eligibility requirements: Be a resident of Accra, Ghana . Be between 16 and 35 years old . Have an existing small-scale green business in areas such as: Waste management Sustainable agriculture Renewable energy Eco-friendly manufacturing Other environmentally sustainable sectors Alternatively, applicants may have a well-developed green business idea within the same sectors. Demonstrate commitment to formalizing and expanding their business or business idea. Be available to attend the complete two-day training programme. Why You Should Apply The Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers offers more than classroom instruction. It provides participants with practical entrepreneurial skills, exposure to experienced professionals, and access to networks that can support long-term business success. Young entrepreneurs working in environmental sustainability often face challenges related to funding, business management, and market access. This programme addresses these challenges by providing targeted training designed specifically for businesses operating within the green economy. Participants will leave the programme with stronger business knowledge, improved financial planning skills, enhanced marketing capabilities, and valuable professional connections that can contribute to the growth of their enterprises. APPLY NOW Important Deadline Applications for the Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers 2026 close on: 14 August 2026 Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. Additional Information The programme is strictly for residents of Accra, Ghana . Attendance for the entire two-day training programme is mandatory. Only selected applicants will receive further communication regarding participation. Conclusion The Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers 2026 presents an excellent opportunity for young entrepreneurs and waste workers in Accra to strengthen their business knowledge, develop practical entrepreneurial skills, and connect with professionals within Ghana s growing green economy. Whether you already operate a sustainable business or have an innovative green business idea, this programme offers valuable training in business development, financial management, digital marketing, grant writing, and networking. Participants will also benefit from mentorship opportunities and receive a certificate upon successful completion. If you meet the eligibility requirements and are committed to building or expanding a green enterprise that contributes to environmental sustainability, be sure to submit your application before the 14 August 2026 deadline. title: Unfunded List Grant Proposal Feedback Program 2026 | Get Expert Reviews Before You Submit
summary: Securing funding often depends on the quality of a grant proposal. However, obtaining meaningful feedback before submitting a proposal can be one of the biggest challenges facing nonprofits, researchers, social enterprises, and community organizations. To address this gap, the Unfunded List Grant Proposal Feedback Program 2026 is inviting organizations and proposal writers to submit their grant applications for expert review and constructive feedback. Rather than providing funding directly, the Unfunded List helps organizations improve their proposals through a structured review process designed to increase competitiveness and strengthen future funding applications. The submission deadline for the current round is September 20, 2026 . About the Unfunded List The Unfunded List is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization committed to demystifying philanthropy through education, collaboration, and feedback. The organization believes that great ideas deserve both feedback and funding. By connecting applicants with experienced evaluators, the Unfunded List creates opportunities for organizations to refine their proposals, strengthen their fundraising strategies, and improve their chances of securing grants. How the Feedback Process Works The Unfunded List follows a structured review process that helps organizations receive thoughtful and actionable feedback. Step 1: Submit Your Proposal Organizations submit an existing grant proposal through the Unfunded List application process. Step 2: Evaluator Assignment Each proposal is assigned to a cohort of reviewers and evaluators with experience in grant assessment and proposal review. Step 3: Proposal Review Evaluators carefully assess the proposal and provide detailed feedback on its strengths, weaknesses, clarity, and competitiveness. Step 4: Feedback Report The individual reviews are compiled into a comprehensive report that highlights key recommendations and opportunities for improvement. Step 5: Feedback Discussion Participants receive an opportunity to discuss the feedback with the Unfunded List team, helping them better understand how to strengthen future submissions. Why Participate? Organizations that participate in the program can benefit from: • Independent review of grant proposals • Constructive and actionable feedback • Insights from experienced evaluators • Improved proposal quality and competitiveness • Increased understanding of funder expectations • Opportunities to strengthen future funding applications • Access to a collaborative learning community Who Can Apply? The program welcomes proposals from a wide range of organizations and applicants. Eligible participants may include: • Nonprofit organizations • Community-based organizations • Social enterprises • Researchers • Educational institutions • Charitable initiatives • International organizations Organizations do not need to be based in the United States to participate. Applicants who have previously received grant funding are also encouraged to apply. Program Cost To ensure active participation and commitment, the Unfunded List charges a modest fee for first-time participants. First-Time Submission Fee • $100 per proposal Future Participation Organizations that fully engage in the review process and participate as evaluators may be invited to submit future proposals at no additional cost. Questions regarding participation fees can be directed to: 📧 dave@unfundedlist.com Benefits of Joining the Learning Community The Unfunded List emphasizes continuous learning and improvement. Organizations that engage repeatedly in the process often gain the greatest benefit. Participants are encouraged to: • Submit proposals in future review rounds • Join evaluator committees • Learn from other proposal writers • Strengthen grant-writing skills over time • Build long-term fundraising capacity Important Dates Proposal Submission Deadline 📅 September 20, 2026 Feedback Delivery 📅 By December 1, 2026 Why Feedback Matters Many organizations invest significant time and effort into preparing grant proposals, yet they rarely receive detailed explanations when applications are unsuccessful. The Unfunded List helps fill this gap by offering a rare opportunity to receive expert insights before resubmitting or pursuing future funding opportunities. Whether your proposal is intended for foundations, government grants, research funding, or philanthropic organizations, thoughtful feedback can help identify areas for improvement and increase the likelihood of future success. Conclusion The Unfunded List Grant Proposal Feedback Program offers a valuable opportunity for nonprofits, researchers, and mission-driven organizations to strengthen their grant applications through expert review and collaborative learning. If you are preparing a funding proposal and would benefit from constructive feedback before your next submission, this program could help improve both your proposal quality and your long-term fundraising strategy. Discover more opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage . title: AERC-World Bank Visiting Scholars Program 2026/2027 for African Researchers
summary: The African Economic Research Consortium (AERC) , in partnership with the World Bank Africa Region Chief Economist’s Office (AFRCE) , is inviting applications for the AERC-World Bank Visiting Scholars Program 2026/2027 . This prestigious fellowship offers African researchers the opportunity to spend between four and six months at the World Bank, collaborate with leading economists, and strengthen research that contributes to Africa’s development agenda. The program is a key component of the collaboration between AERC and the World Bank aimed at enhancing economic policy research, strengthening academic networks, and increasing the policy impact of research across Sub-Saharan Africa. Applications are open until September 6, 2026 . About the AERC-World Bank Visiting Scholars Program The Visiting Scholars Program was established under a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between AERC and the World Bank’s Africa Region Chief Economist’s Office. Through this initiative, selected scholars gain access to the World Bank’s extensive research resources, professional networks, and analytical expertise. The fellowship is designed to support African researchers working on development-focused economic research while fostering stronger collaboration between African scholars and World Bank researchers. Program Objectives The collaboration seeks to: • Enhance AERC’s capacity to strengthen economic policy research in Sub-Saharan Africa. • Strengthen global academic and policy linkages for AERC researchers. • Increase the policy influence and impact of research conducted by both AERC and the World Bank. • Improve the research output, publication record, and teaching capacity of African researchers through access to World Bank resources, data, and networks. Fellowship Benefits Selected visiting scholars will have the opportunity to: • Spend four to six months at the World Bank. • Work closely with researchers in the Office of the Chief Economist for Africa Region (DECAF). • Access world-class research resources, datasets, and analytical tools. • Participate in capacity-building activities organized by the World Bank. • Collaborate with scholars contributing to Africa Regional Flagship Studies. • Strengthen professional networks with leading economists and development experts. • Revise and improve research papers for submission to high-ranking academic journals and the World Bank Working Paper Series. • Present research findings through seminars and academic discussions. • Enhance course materials and academic content for university teaching. Responsibilities of Visiting Scholars During the fellowship period, scholars will be expected to: • Participate actively in DECAF-led activities. • Engage with World Bank researchers and analytical teams. • Revise and strengthen their draft research papers. • Submit research outputs to the World Bank Working Paper Series and peer-reviewed journals. • Deliver at least one seminar presentation on their research. • Contribute to ongoing analytical and research activities within the World Bank Africa Region. • Develop a repository of research interests and areas of expertise. • Comply with all program requirements and consultancy contract obligations. Eligibility Criteria Applicants must: • Be an AERC researcher, including participants in the AERC Collaborative PhD Programme (CPP). • Have an active AERC research project at the interim, post-fieldwork, or final research paper stage. • Be conducting research relevant to the World Bank Africa Region’s research priorities and Africa’s development challenges. Encouraged Applicants Women researchers, as well as francophone and lusophone candidates, are especially encouraged to apply. Required Application Documents Applicants must submit: • A two-page statement of interest. • A draft research paper addressing issues relevant to African development and the World Bank Africa Region research agenda. • Relevant curriculum or course materials they wish to improve during the fellowship (if applicable). • An updated Curriculum Vitae (CV). How to Apply Application packages should be submitted via email to: 📧 abbi.kedir@aercafrica.org Copy: 📧 research@aercafrica.org Applicants should ensure all required documents are included before submission. Number of Awards Up to two awards will be offered for the 2026/2027 cohort . Application Deadline 📅 September 6, 2026 Late applications will not be considered. Why You Should Apply The AERC-World Bank Visiting Scholars Program offers a rare opportunity for African researchers to deepen their research expertise, engage directly with leading development economists, and contribute to policy-relevant work addressing Africa’s most pressing economic challenges. By combining access to global research resources with opportunities for publication, networking, and professional development, the fellowship can significantly enhance both academic and policy impact. Final Thoughts If you are an AERC researcher working on issues related to economic development in Africa, this fellowship provides an excellent platform to strengthen your research, expand your professional network, and contribute to evidence-based policymaking across the continent. Researchers with strong ongoing projects and a commitment to advancing African development are encouraged to apply before the deadline. Discover more fellowship opportunities on the OFY Webpage . title: Fully Funded AI Safety Research Positions at Hasso Plattner Institute 2026: PhD, Postdoctoral and Research Internship Opportunities in Germany
summary: Applications and expressions of interest are now being accepted for several full-time research positions in the new AI Safety and Societal Impacts Research Group at the Hasso Plattner Institute , commonly known as HPI, in Potsdam/Berlin, Germany. The new research group will be led by Dr Paul Röttger , an AI safety researcher whose work focuses on large language models, AI evaluation, political and social bias, AI alignment and the broader societal consequences of artificial intelligence. The available opportunities include: A three-year, fully funded PhD position A postdoctoral research position lasting one to two years A research internship lasting three to six months All positions are full-time and require participants to be based in Germany. Group members will normally be expected to work from the office two or three days per week, with flexibility for the remaining working days. Appointments are expected to begin in or after September 2026 . Expressions of interest are being reviewed on a rolling basis, and no fixed application deadline has been announced. Interested candidates should therefore apply as early as possible. About the AI Safety and Societal Impacts Research Group The new research group will be established at the Hasso Plattner Institute in Potsdam, part of the Berlin metropolitan region. Its mission is based on the understanding that artificial intelligence systems are becoming increasingly capable, widely adopted and deeply integrated into people’s personal, professional, social and political lives. These developments offer significant potential benefits, but they may also create serious risks. The research group will study these risks and benefits with the aim of contributing to better and safer outcomes from artificial intelligence. The group plans to conduct research that can influence: Artificial intelligence research AI system development Public and academic discussions about AI Technology governance Public policy Safety practices Technical approaches to risk mitigation The initiative is supported through the German Research Foundation’s Emmy Noether Programme. Dr Röttger has stated that the research group is funded for six years. The German Research Foundation lists his project as “AI Methods for Measuring and Mitigating Political Bias in AI Systems.” German Research Foundation Available Research Positions Applicants can express interest in one of three positions. Fully Funded PhD Position The PhD position will have a duration of three years and is expressly described as fully funded. This opportunity may be suitable for candidates who want to undertake doctoral research on AI safety, natural language processing, AI evaluation, computational social science or the societal impacts of artificial intelligence. A successful PhD researcher would be expected to develop an original research agenda while contributing to the wider mission of the group. The official announcement does not specify: The exact salary or monthly funding amount Tuition-fee arrangements A mandatory academic degree Required grade thresholds A compulsory list of programming languages English or German language test requirements Relocation support Travel funding Health insurance arrangements Applicants should not assume these benefits or requirements unless they are subsequently confirmed by HPI or the group leader. Postdoctoral Research Position Postdoctoral appointments will be available for a period of one to two years. This position is likely intended for researchers who have completed, or are close to completing, a PhD in a relevant field. However, the expression-of-interest form does not provide a detailed formal eligibility statement or specify when the doctoral degree must be completed. Potentially relevant backgrounds may include: Computer science Artificial intelligence Machine learning Natural language processing Computational social science Human-computer interaction Political science Psychology Sociology Communication studies Technology policy AI governance Other related disciplines Applicants should demonstrate how their research experience connects with the group’s focus on capable AI systems and their integration into social and political processes. Research Internship Research internships will last between three and six months. The internship is full-time and in person. Interns will be expected to work from the office for approximately two or three days each week, with the remaining schedule offering some flexibility. The form does not specify: Whether applicants must be enrolled at a university A minimum or maximum academic level Whether undergraduate students can apply Whether a master’s degree is required The internship salary or stipend Accommodation or relocation support Visa sponsorship arrangements Candidates who are interested in the internship should submit an expression of interest and allow the group to determine whether their experience and research interests are suitable. Location and Working Arrangement All positions will be based at the Hasso Plattner Institute in Potsdam/Berlin, Germany. The positions are not advertised as fully remote opportunities. Applicants must be willing and able to relocate or regularly attend the institute in person. The stated working arrangement is: Full-time participation In-person attendance Approximately two or three office days per week Flexible arrangements for the remaining working days International candidates should consider relocation and visa requirements before applying. The form asks applicants to state their nationality specifically for possible visa-related purposes, indicating that immigration arrangements may be considered later in the recruitment process. However, applicants should not interpret this as a confirmed guarantee of visa sponsorship. The availability and terms of immigration support must be verified directly with the institute if the application progresses. Expected Starting Date The research group will begin operating from September 2026 . Positions may begin in September 2026 or at a later mutually agreed date. Every applicant must provide their earliest possible starting date in the expression-of-interest form. Candidates should enter a realistic date after considering: Current academic or employment obligations Notice periods Thesis submission or defence schedules Graduation dates Visa processing Relocation arrangements Personal commitments Applicants are not instructed to select September if they cannot realistically begin at that time. The wording “starting in or after September 2026” indicates some flexibility. Main Research Areas The group will investigate the risks and benefits that emerge when highly capable artificial intelligence systems become integrated into important social and political processes. Examples of relevant processes include: Public communication Political discourse Human coordination Contract negotiation Competition between digital services Delegation of decisions to AI agents Interaction between multiple autonomous AI systems Influence of AI-generated information on public opinion The group expects to combine technical and social-science research methods. Model Evaluations Researchers may design evaluations to measure how artificial intelligence systems behave under different conditions. This could involve studying: Political or ideological bias Safety failures Manipulative behaviour Misalignment Reliability Influence on users Behaviour in multi-agent environments Differences between controlled evaluations and real-world deployment Computational Experiments Computational experiments may be used to test hypotheses about AI behaviour at scale. These studies could examine how artificial intelligence systems: Respond to competing incentives Interact with other agents Adapt to markets and audiences Influence information environments Develop or reproduce problematic behaviour Perform when given delegated responsibilities Human Studies Human studies may be used to understand how people interact with AI systems and how AI-generated content affects human beliefs, decisions, coordination and behaviour. This may include controlled experiments involving: AI-assisted writing Human trust in AI Political communication Persuasion Negotiation Decision-making Emotional responses User dependence on AI-generated advice Technical Mitigations Where possible, the group will develop technical approaches to reduce or manage identified risks. These interventions could include: Improved evaluation frameworks Bias-detection methods Behavioural monitoring tools Model safeguards Oversight mechanisms Multi-agent safety evaluations Methods for tracing the origins of model behaviour Controls for AI systems operating in dynamic environments Illustrative Research Challenges The application form provides three examples of the research problems the group may investigate. Political and Social Bias in AI Systems Artificial intelligence systems may influence public opinion when they assist users with writing, research or decision-making. For example, an AI writing assistant responding to questions about AI governance may present information in a politically biased or ideologically unbalanced way. Because users may rely on these systems for information and communication, such bias could shape public discourse. Potential research questions include: How can political bias in AI systems be measured reliably? How can researchers distinguish model bias from user preferences or training-data patterns? How does AI-assisted writing influence public attitudes? Where do problematic biases originate? What technical interventions can reduce these biases? Can mitigation methods work across languages, cultures and political contexts? Delegation to AI Agents People and organizations may increasingly delegate coordination tasks to autonomous AI agents. For example, AI systems may negotiate contracts, manage schedules, coordinate transactions or communicate with other AI agents on behalf of users. This could create new risks if an agent: Misunderstands its user’s intentions Pursues the wrong objective Makes commitments without sufficient oversight Coordinates harmfully with another agent Behaves strategically or deceptively Prioritizes measurable outcomes over human interests The group wants to understand the consequences of delegating important human responsibilities to interacting AI systems and to evaluate misalignment in multi-agent settings. Spread of Misaligned Behaviour AI agents may compete for customers, audiences, engagement or economic rewards. In such environments, harmful behaviours could spread if they provide a competitive advantage. An emotionally manipulative AI system, for example, could attract more attention or user engagement, encouraging competing systems to adopt similar behaviour. Research in this area may investigate: How harmful strategies emerge How behaviours transfer between AI agents Whether market competition amplifies misalignment How AI systems learn after deployment How humans can maintain oversight What controls are effective in real-world environments Research Culture The group aims to combine research impact with an enjoyable and intellectually open working environment. Its stated cultural principles include: Impactful Research The group wants its work to influence AI research, system development, policy, public discourse and responsible technology practices. Researchers should be interested in questions that matter beyond a narrow academic setting. Individual Exploration Group members will be encouraged to explore their own ideas and develop intrinsic research motivation. Candidates should be able to identify important questions rather than depend entirely on assigned tasks. Creativity The group values original thinking and new methods for studying emerging AI risks and benefits. Collaboration Members will work collaboratively, support one another and contribute to a shared research environment both in person and online. Open Research The group intends to share its work openly. Candidates should be comfortable with transparent research practices and constructive engagement with the wider research community. Epistemic Humility Researchers will be expected to question their assumptions, recognize uncertainty and revise their conclusions when stronger evidence becomes available. Adaptation to New Knowledge Artificial intelligence is developing quickly. The group expects to adjust its methods and research priorities as models, applications and scientific knowledge evolve. Ideal Candidate Profile Dr Röttger’s accompanying recruitment announcement states that ideal candidates will have a background somewhere between computer science or natural language processing and the social sciences. Strong candidates are also expected to: Be genuinely interested in contemporary AI developments Care about generating positive societal impact Be motivated by open research Think seriously about both AI risks and AI benefits Be able to formulate concrete research questions Understand the relationship between technology and society Demonstrate curiosity and intellectual independence Be willing to challenge their own assumptions Work collaboratively with researchers from different disciplines Be able to relocate to or work regularly in Potsdam/Berlin The opportunity may be particularly relevant to candidates working at the intersection of: Computer science and political science Natural language processing and social science AI evaluation and public policy Machine learning and human behaviour AI alignment and computational social science AI safety and communication studies Technical research and technology governance The recruitment announcement does not limit applications to candidates who fit one precise disciplinary profile. Interdisciplinary backgrounds may be particularly valuable. About Dr Paul Röttger Dr Paul Röttger is an AI researcher specializing in the evaluation and improvement of large language model safety and the study of AI’s societal impacts. His research interests include: AI safety AI risks AI evaluation AI alignment Large language model bias Societal impacts of AI Hate-speech detection Political bias in AI systems He earned a DPhil from the University of Oxford and has worked with the Oxford Internet Institute and the UK AI Security Institute. His research has received an Outstanding Paper Award at ACL and a Best Paper Award at NeurIPS. About Hasso Plattner Institute The Hasso Plattner Institute is a university-level digital engineering and computer science institution located in Potsdam, Germany. HPI conducts teaching and research in fields connected with digital engineering, computer science and information technology. The new AI Safety and Societal Impacts Research Group will form part of this broader research environment. Information Required in the Expression-of-Interest Form Applicants must provide the following information: Full name Email address Current role and institutional affiliation Position of interest Earliest available starting date Nationality Publicly accessible link to a CV Explanation of the concrete AI risk or risks that concern them most Explanation of the concrete AI benefit or benefits that excite them most Description of a hypothetical three-month research project Any additional information they want the group leader to consider The final additional-information question is optional. The main application questions are mandatory. Written Application Questions AI Risks Question Applicants must answer: Which concrete risk or risks from AI are you most concerned about and why? The answer must remain within 500 characters , approximately 100 words. Candidates should focus on a specific risk rather than discussing AI safety only in broad terms. Possible subjects might include: Political persuasion Model manipulation AI-enabled misinformation Multi-agent misalignment Loss of human oversight Bias in AI-assisted communication Emotional exploitation Autonomous decision-making Security failures Harmful competition between AI systems Applicants should select issues that genuinely reflect their own research interests. AI Benefits Question Applicants must answer: Which concrete benefit or benefits from AI are you most excited about and why? This answer is also limited to 500 characters , approximately 100 words. Applicants should demonstrate that they can evaluate artificial intelligence in a balanced manner. The group is interested in both risks and benefits, not only in pessimistic or alarmist perspectives. Three-Month Research Project Question Applicants must describe the research project they would start if they were beginning a three-month project immediately. The response is limited to 1,000 characters , approximately 200 words. The project is hypothetical and is used to understand the applicant’s research interests. A strong project description should briefly communicate: The problem The research question Why the issue matters The proposed method The data, models or participants involved The expected output How the project relates to AI safety or societal impacts Applicants should propose something realistic enough to investigate within three months. CV-Link Requirement Applicants must provide a link to their CV rather than upload the document directly. The link must be accessible to anyone who opens it. Candidates should test the link in a private or incognito browser window before submitting it. The CV should ideally highlight: Education Research experience Publications Technical skills Programming experience Research methods Relevant employment AI safety projects Social-science research Awards Open-source contributions Links to publications, code repositories or personal research pages Important Instruction About Artificial Intelligence The form explicitly asks candidates not to use AI to complete their application responses . Dr Röttger states that he wants to learn about applicants and their interests in their own words. Candidates should therefore write the application independently. AI-generated answers may fail to represent the candidate’s genuine thinking and could conflict with the express instruction provided by the research-group leader. Prospective applicants may review publicly available information to understand the programme, but their submitted answers should be original, personal and written without generative-AI assistance. Application Deadline and Review Process No fixed closing date is stated. Applications are considered on a rolling basis , meaning submissions may be reviewed as they arrive. The form asks applicants to allow approximately two to four weeks for processing. Because recruitment is rolling and positions may be filled progressively, early submission is advisable. Applicants should not wait for a final deadline to be announced. How to Submit an Expression of Interest To apply: Open the official expression-of-interest form . Review the group’s mission, research priorities and working culture. Select the PhD, postdoctoral or research-intern position. Enter your earliest possible starting date. Provide an accessible link to your CV. Write your responses independently and in your own words. Keep each response within the stated character limit. Review all information carefully. Submit the form. Allow approximately two to four weeks for processing. Conclusion The new AI Safety and Societal Impacts Research Group at Hasso Plattner Institute offers a significant opportunity for researchers interested in understanding how increasingly capable AI systems affect communication, coordination, competition and other essential social and political processes. With fully funded doctoral research, postdoctoral appointments and research internships available, the group is seeking candidates capable of combining technical knowledge with an understanding of society and human behaviour. The positions are particularly relevant to researchers working across computer science, natural language processing, AI evaluation and the social sciences. Successful candidates will join a collaborative and open research environment focused on producing work that can influence academic research, system development, policy and public discourse. There is no fixed closing date, but applications are being assessed on a rolling basis. Interested candidates should therefore prepare their CV, develop their own authentic responses and submit the expression-of-interest form as early as possible. title: Prime Minister’s National Youth Council 2026: Applications Open for Batch 4 to Shape Pakistan’s Future
summary: Applications are now open for Batch 4 of the Prime Minister’s National Youth Council 2026, offering young Pakistanis a national platform to participate in policy dialogue, highlight issues affecting youth and contribute ideas for the country’s development. The National Youth Council, commonly known as the NYC, operates under the Prime Minister’s Youth Programme. It is intended to connect young leaders with public institutions and create meaningful opportunities for youth participation in decision-making. Selected members will receive a two-year opportunity to contribute their knowledge, community experience and recommendations to policy discussions at the federal and provincial levels. Applications must be submitted by 15 August 2026 through the Prime Minister’s Digital Youth Hub. The latest application announcement was shared by UN Women Pakistan, which invited young people between the ages of 15 and 29 from across Pakistan to apply. The wider PMYP announcement also covers applicants from Pakistan’s provinces and territories and the overseas Pakistani diaspora. UN Women Pakistan announcement About the Prime Minister’s National Youth Council The Prime Minister’s National Youth Council is a youth advisory and engagement platform operating under the Prime Minister’s Youth Programme. Its central purpose is to involve young people in national policymaking and provide them with an organized channel through which they can raise important issues affecting Pakistan’s youth. The council brings together young people who have demonstrated leadership, commitment to their communities, professional or social achievements, and a desire to contribute to Pakistan’s development. According to the official Digital Youth Hub, the council is intended to: Involve youth in the country’s policymaking processes. Enable young people to identify and highlight key youth-related issues. Bring together talented and committed individuals from different backgrounds. Promote youth participation in national development. Provide policy support to provincial youth ministries. Develop an official consortium or network of youth organizations. Support the institutional development of the National Youth Council. Establish a digital platform for youth engagement, dialogue and the presentation of inspiring work. The council is therefore more than a ceremonial youth body. It functions as a platform through which young people can communicate their concerns, propose solutions and contribute to discussions concerning Pakistan’s social and economic future. Official National Youth Council page What Is the Purpose of the National Youth Council? Pakistan has a large and diverse youth population. However, young people may not always have direct access to the institutions responsible for designing and implementing national and provincial policies. The National Youth Council seeks to reduce this gap by establishing a formal relationship between young citizens and government institutions. Its work is focused on several interconnected purposes. 1. Youth Participation in Policymaking The council enables young people to share recommendations and perspectives on matters that directly affect them. This may include issues such as: Education and access to learning Employment and decent work Entrepreneurship Digital inclusion Climate change and environmental action Skills development Gender equality Social inclusion Youth health and well-being Innovation and emerging technologies Civic participation Community development Sports, arts and culture The official Digital Youth Hub describes the National Youth Council as a mechanism for involving youth in policymaking and enabling them to highlight the major challenges young people face. Digital Youth Hub engagement page 2. Policy Advice to Government The National Youth Council serves as a youth advisory platform. Its members may provide input, recommendations and ideas concerning youth-centered policies and programmes. The council is intended to help policymakers understand how national decisions affect young people from different regions and social backgrounds. 3. Representation of Pakistan’s Diverse Youth An effective national youth platform must represent more than one city, educational institution, profession or social group. Batch 4 is open to eligible young people representing: Punjab Sindh Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Balochistan Islamabad Capital Territory Azad Jammu and Kashmir Gilgit-Baltistan Overseas Pakistani communities The programme encourages inclusive representation. Young women, transgender persons, persons with disabilities, religious minorities and candidates from different social, professional and community backgrounds are encouraged to participate. 4. Identification of Youth Issues Council members can help bring local and regional concerns to national attention. For example, a young person working in climate action may highlight environmental risks facing a particular community. A technology innovator may propose ways to improve digital access, while a community worker may identify barriers affecting education, employment or social inclusion. This diversity allows the council to obtain a more realistic understanding of the challenges experienced by Pakistani youth. 5. Development of Youth-Led Solutions The council is also intended to move beyond identifying problems. Members may help formulate practical recommendations and youth-led approaches to addressing development challenges. This can support: Evidence-based youth policies Community-focused interventions Youth consultation mechanisms Digital engagement initiatives Inclusive leadership programmes Collaboration among youth organizations Stronger communication between young citizens and policymakers Duration of the Opportunity Selected members of Batch 4 are expected to serve for a two-year tenure . During this period, council members may participate in engagement, consultation and policy-support activities connected with the Prime Minister’s Youth Programme and other relevant institutions. Applicants should therefore treat the council as a serious medium-term commitment rather than a one-time event. Candidates should be prepared to participate responsibly, contribute ideas, communicate professionally and represent the concerns of young people. Why Should Young People Apply? Membership in the Prime Minister’s National Youth Council provides an opportunity to contribute to national development through a recognized government-led platform. Potential advantages of participation include: Direct Engagement with Policy Issues Members can contribute their views on policies and programmes affecting young people. This offers them an opportunity to connect their community experience with national-level discussions. National Representation Participants may represent the perspectives of young people from their province, territory, professional field, social group or overseas community. Leadership Experience A two-year council tenure may strengthen participants’ experience in leadership, policy dialogue, consultation, advocacy, teamwork and institutional engagement. Networking and Collaboration Members may interact with other young leaders, government representatives, youth organizations, development partners and professionals working in different sectors. Opportunity to Raise Community Concerns Council members may bring attention to challenges faced by young people in underserved areas or underrepresented communities. Contribution to Inclusive Development The initiative provides a platform for young people to contribute to conversations about sustainable development, social inclusion, education, employment, climate resilience, technology and other national priorities. Applicants should note, however, that the available announcement does not specifically promise a salary, stipend, travel allowance, employment, scholarship funding or monetary award . Candidates should rely only on benefits expressly confirmed through the official application portal. Who Is the Ideal Applicant? The programme may be particularly suitable for young people who: Have demonstrated leadership in their institution, profession or community. Are actively involved in volunteer work or community service. Work on education, health, technology, climate action or social inclusion. Lead a youth organization, initiative, campaign or social enterprise. Have experience identifying and addressing community challenges. Are interested in public policy, governance or civic participation. Can represent the concerns of young people from their region or community. Are committed to Pakistan’s social and economic development. Can communicate ideas clearly and work with people from diverse backgrounds. Are prepared to participate throughout the two-year tenure. Applicants may come from fields including, but not limited to: Education Entrepreneurship Technology Science and research Climate and environmental action Arts and culture Sports Media and communications Social development Public policy Volunteerism Disability inclusion Gender equality Community development Health Agriculture Business and industry No particular profession or academic discipline has been identified as the sole route to eligibility. Inclusion and Equal Participation The National Youth Council is intended to reflect the diversity of Pakistan’s youth. The published announcement highlights equitable participation for: Women Transgender persons Persons with disabilities Religious minorities Young people from different provincial and regional backgrounds Members of the overseas Pakistani diaspora Individuals from different professional, educational and social backgrounds This means eligible applicants should not assume that selection is limited to university students, government employees, established professionals or nationally recognized personalities. Community organizers, volunteers, emerging leaders, students, entrepreneurs, activists, artists, innovators and young professionals may all be relevant candidates if they satisfy the official requirements and demonstrate meaningful leadership potential. Application Deadline The deadline for submitting an application is: 15 August 2026 Applicants should complete the process before the closing date. Waiting until the final day may create avoidable problems, particularly if the platform becomes busy or additional information is required. How to Apply for the National Youth Council Batch 4 Applications must be submitted through the Prime Minister’s Digital Youth Hub. Follow these steps: Visit the Prime Minister’s Youth Programme website . Create an account or sign in to the Digital Youth Hub. Open the Engagement section. Locate the National Youth Council opportunity. Review the official eligibility requirements and application instructions. Select the option to apply. Complete all required sections of the application form. Upload any documents requested by the portal. Review the information for errors or omissions. Submit the application before 15 August 2026. Save a screenshot or confirmation message as proof of submission. Applicants may also access the opportunity through the Digital Youth Hub mobile application, subject to its availability and functionality. Information Applicants Should Prepare Although the exact fields must be confirmed on the application portal, applicants should generally be ready to provide: Full legal name Date of birth CNIC, NICOP or other requested identification Contact information Province, territory or country of residence Educational background Professional or volunteer experience Leadership roles Community involvement Achievements and recognitions Areas of interest or expertise Reasons for joining the National Youth Council Information about issues affecting youth in their community Proposed ideas or recommendations Supporting documents, if requested Applicants should enter information accurately. Details relating to age, identity and residence should match the documents used during the application process. Tips for Preparing a Strong Application Demonstrate Real Leadership Leadership does not necessarily mean holding a senior title. Applicants can demonstrate leadership by explaining how they initiated an activity, organized people, addressed a community issue or delivered measurable results. Provide Specific Evidence Avoid unsupported statements such as “I am passionate about youth empowerment.” Instead, describe: What you did Why you did it Who benefited How many people were involved What changed because of your work What you learned from the experience Connect Experience with Policy Applicants should explain how their experience could help the council understand and address youth-related issues. For example, someone working on waste reduction could connect that experience with climate policy, green employment and community awareness. A technology professional could discuss digital access, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity or online safety. Represent More Than Yourself A strong candidate should be able to explain the challenges faced by other young people in their community, province, sector or social group. The council is a representative platform. Applications focused only on personal career advancement may be less persuasive than those demonstrating a genuine commitment to broader youth development. Propose Practical Solutions Where the application asks for ideas, candidates should present realistic recommendations rather than broad slogans. A strong proposal should identify: The problem The people affected The proposed intervention The institutions that could participate The expected results A practical method for implementation Highlight Inclusion Applicants who have worked with women, persons with disabilities, minorities, rural communities or other underrepresented groups should explain this experience clearly. Review Before Submission Applicants should check: Names and identification details Dates Contact information Grammar and spelling Supporting documents Word or character limits Completeness of every required section Important Points to Remember Applications are open for Batch 4 of the Prime Minister’s National Youth Council. The programme is designed for young people aged 15–29. The opportunity has a two-year tenure. Eligible applicants can come from across Pakistan, its territories and the overseas Pakistani diaspora. The council supports youth engagement in policymaking. Applications must be submitted through the Digital Youth Hub. The deadline is 15 August 2026. Applicants should verify all final requirements directly through the official portal. No confirmed salary, stipend or monetary award is stated in the published announcement. Conclusion The Prime Minister’s National Youth Council Batch 4 provides young Pakistanis with an important opportunity to bring youth perspectives into national and provincial policy discussions. For applicants already involved in leadership, community service, entrepreneurship, technology, climate action, education, advocacy, arts, sports or social development, the council offers a structured platform to transform practical experience into policy recommendations. Successful participation will require more than enthusiasm. Applicants should demonstrate credible leadership, awareness of youth challenges, the ability to represent diverse communities and a genuine commitment to public service. Eligible candidates should prepare a clear, evidence-based application and submit it through the Digital Youth Hub before 15 August 2026 . For more global opportunities, click HERE.
