title: Capital One Summer 2027 Internships: Apply for the Technology and Cyber Security Internship Programs
summary: Applications are now open for two paid Capital One Summer 2027 internship programmes in the United States: the Technology Internship Program and the Cyber Security Internship Program . Both opportunities are designed for students pursuing bachelor’s degrees or higher who want to gain practical experience inside a major financial institution operating as a technology-driven company. The internships combine hands-on project work, professional training, mentorship, networking and exposure to senior leaders. Each programme runs for ten weeks from June through August 2027 . Interns must remain in the continental United States and attend their assigned office in person in accordance with Capital One’s hybrid working model. Capital One has indicated that each vacancy is expected to remain open for at least five business days. However, because of high interest, the listings may close quickly. Eligible students are therefore strongly encouraged to apply as early as possible. Overview of the Capital One Summer 2027 Internships The two available programmes are: Capital One Technology Internship Program – Summer 2027 Capital One Cyber Security Internship Program – Summer 2027 Both are: Full-time Paid Ten weeks long Scheduled from June to August 2027 Based in the continental United States Conducted under Capital One’s hybrid working model Intended for students continuing their studies after the internship Connected to possible future full-time opportunities The two programmes share several eligibility requirements, but they provide different professional experiences. The Technology Internship Program focuses primarily on software engineering, cloud technologies, artificial intelligence, application development and modern engineering practices. The Cyber Security Internship Program focuses on network defence, security engineering, cyber risk, cloud and application security, incident response, digital forensics and related cybersecurity functions. About Capital One Capital One is a financial-services company that describes itself as the kind of bank a technology company would build. The organisation uses software engineering, artificial intelligence, machine learning, cloud computing and data to develop products that help millions of customers manage their finances. Capital One’s technology environment includes areas such as: Cloud infrastructure Open-source technologies RESTful application programming interfaces Microservices Containers Artificial intelligence Machine learning Web and mobile development Cybersecurity Data engineering Software platforms The company develops many of its own products and places a strong emphasis on rapid experimentation, product ownership and continuous improvement. Interns will enter an environment where engineers and cybersecurity professionals work on systems that support large numbers of customers and process significant volumes of financial and operational data. Capital One Technology Internship Program – Summer 2027 The Technology Internship Program is a ten-week paid programme for students interested in software engineering and technology. It is available in: McLean, Virginia Richmond, Virginia Plano, Texas The programme gives interns an opportunity to contribute to technical projects while developing a broader understanding of engineering at Capital One. What Technology Interns May Work On Technology interns may work on projects involving: Customer-facing web applications Mobile applications Back-end systems Highly available RESTful services Cloud platforms Big-data technologies Full-stack development Developer productivity Artificial intelligence-assisted coding Software testing and quality Infrastructure and deployment Capital One describes its engineering model as a “You Build It, You Own It” environment. This means engineering teams may be involved not only in creating software but also in maintaining, improving and supporting it after deployment. The technology stack mentioned in the internship description includes: Java React Angular Vue.js C# REST APIs NoSQL databases Kubernetes Terraform Jenkins Docker Amazon Web Services Scala Clojure Haskell C++ Go Scheme Common Lisp Artificial intelligence-powered development tools The exact tools used by each intern will depend on the assigned team and project. Applicants are not necessarily expected to have experience with every technology listed. Technology Internship Experience During the ten-week Technology Internship Program, interns can expect: A challenging engineering assignment Collaboration with diverse technical teams Exposure to artificial intelligence coding tools Opportunities to improve development speed and code quality Executive speaker sessions Interaction with senior leadership Technical training and development sessions Social and networking events Volunteer activities with other interns Training topics may include: iOS development Android development Web development Amazon Web Services Open-source big-data tools Cybersecurity Voice-driven applications Software engineering practices Technology interns also receive access to Capital One’s Tech College, an internal learning platform providing online and in-person instruction. Its learning areas include: Cloud computing Cybersecurity Data Machine learning and artificial intelligence Mobile development Software engineering Technology Internship Basic Qualifications Applicants must: Be pursuing a bachelor’s degree or higher Expect to complete their most recent full-time degree programme by August 2028 or earlier Continue in the same course of study after completing the internship Provide formal academic documentation confirming their expected graduation date when requested The “most recent full-time degree programme” rule is important. For example, a student completing a bachelor’s degree in May 2027 who is already enrolled in a full-time master’s programme ending in May 2028 would be assessed based on the master’s programme. Applicants must still be enrolled in and continuing that same programme after the internship ends. Preferred Qualifications for Technology Applicants Capital One prefers applicants pursuing degrees in technical or quantitative disciplines, including: Computer science Computer engineering Information systems Information technology Mathematics Related technical fields Strong applicants may demonstrate: Analytical ability Quantitative reasoning Problem-solving skills Conceptual thinking Interpersonal skills Leadership potential Written and verbal communication skills Programming experience may include one or more of the following: Go Kotlin Python Java HTML Swift PHP XML JSON UML JavaScript SQL PL/SQL Shell scripting Objective-C C# C C++ Perl .NET ASP.NET Visual Basic Experience using interactive artificial intelligence tools to improve productivity is also preferred. Capital One specifically refers to experience extending beyond basic code completion. Technology Internship Locations and Pay The listing provides the following annualised salary rates: McLean, Virginia: $140,000 Plano, Texas: $127,000 Richmond, Virginia: $127,000 These figures are stated as annual salary rates for the relevant locations. Since the internship lasts ten weeks, actual internship earnings would correspond to the period worked rather than the entire annual amount. The final compensation will be confirmed in the candidate’s offer letter. Technology Internship and Future Employment Technology interns will be evaluated for possible full-time positions within Capital One’s rotational programmes. Potential full-time start dates may fall between six months and one year after completion of the internship. Participation in the internship does not automatically guarantee a full-time offer. Performance, organisational requirements and programme criteria will likely influence any subsequent decision. How to Apply for the Technology Internship Program Applicants should apply through the official Capital One careers page. Technology Internship Program – Summer 2027 Candidates should be prepared to provide an unofficial transcript, degree audit or another formal school record confirming their current expected graduation date. Capital One Cyber Security Internship Program – Summer 2027 The Cyber Security Internship Program is a ten-week paid programme for students interested in cybersecurity, technology risk and the protection of complex digital systems. It is offered in: McLean, Virginia Plano, Texas Cyber interns work with Capital One cybersecurity professionals on practical challenges affecting cloud infrastructure, networks, platforms, applications and data. What Cyber Security Interns May Work On Cyber interns may contribute to projects involving one or more cybersecurity domains. Possible areas include: Cloud security Network security Platform security Application security Cybersecurity data analysis Security automation Network defence System monitoring Vulnerability assessment Offensive security Cyber risk assessment Security engineering Incident response Malware analysis Digital forensics Security intelligence Interns may analyse systems, applications and networks for vulnerabilities or weaknesses and help develop recommendations for strengthening Capital One’s cybersecurity. The programme is designed to give students exposure to several cybersecurity areas before they decide whether to specialise. Cyber Security Internship Experience During the ten-week programme, cyber interns can expect: A practical cybersecurity assignment Collaboration with experienced cybersecurity professionals Mentorship Training through meetups, conferences and technical talks Exposure to technology and cybersecurity executives Opportunities to build a professional network Experience with different tools and technologies Possible rotation across cybersecurity functions Social and volunteer events with other interns Professional-development topics may include: Networking Software development Systems engineering Financial analysis Risk analysis Security intelligence Cloud technologies Cybersecurity operations Cyber interns also receive access to Capital One’s Tech College. The relevant learning disciplines include: Agile methods Cloud computing Cybersecurity Data Machine learning and artificial intelligence Mobile development Software engineering Cyber Security Internship Basic Qualifications Applicants must: Be pursuing a bachelor’s degree or higher Expect to complete their most recent full-time degree programme by August 2028 or earlier Continue in the same course of study after the internship Be available for the ten-week programme from June through August 2027 Students must remain enrolled in their most recent full-time degree programme after the internship. A student who will have completed all studies before the internship ends may therefore not meet this requirement. Preferred Academic Background for Cyber Applicants Capital One prefers candidates studying a technical or quantitative discipline such as: Computer science Computer engineering Cybersecurity Information assurance Information systems Information technology Mathematics A related field Applicants from other academic disciplines may still be considered if they meet the basic requirements and can demonstrate relevant technical knowledge and interest. Preferred Cybersecurity Knowledge Strong candidates may have a basic understanding of: Cybersecurity principles Computer networks Digital forensics Windows macOS Linux Encryption Firewalls Authentication Perimeter protection Network-security protocols Relevant coursework may include: Information-technology fundamentals Cloud security Cryptography Network security Data security Knowledge of established cybersecurity frameworks is also preferred, including: NIST Cybersecurity Framework MITRE ATT CK Applicants may strengthen their applications through hands-on projects or coursework involving: Digital forensics Malware analysis Incident response Vulnerability analysis Security monitoring Network defence Programming Skills for Cyber Applicants Basic programming experience in one or more of the following areas is preferred: Java Python C# C C++ JSON SQL PL/SQL Shell scripting Applicants should also demonstrate analytical, quantitative and problem-solving abilities. Interpersonal, leadership and communication skills are important because cybersecurity work requires collaboration across technical and non-technical teams. As with the Technology Internship Program, experience using interactive artificial intelligence tools beyond basic code completion is preferred. Cyber Security Internship Locations and Pay The listing provides the following annualised salary rates: McLean, Virginia: $140,000 Plano, Texas: $127,000 The internship lasts ten weeks. The figures are annualised rates, and the final compensation for the internship period will be stated in the selected candidate’s offer letter. Cyber Internship and Future Employment Cyber Security Internship Program participants will be evaluated for potential full-time roles within Capital One’s rotational programmes. The relevant full-time start date would generally be one year after completion of the internship. As with the technology programme, successful completion of the internship does not guarantee a full-time offer. How to Apply for the Cyber Security Internship Program Applications should be submitted through the official Capital One careers page. Cyber Security Internship Program – Summer 2027 Candidates should submit their applications as early as possible because of the high volume of expected interest. Requirements Shared by Both Internship Programs Both programmes require applicants to: Pursue a bachelor’s degree or higher Expect to finish their most recent full-time degree programme by August 2028 or earlier Continue studying in the same programme after the internship Participate full-time for ten weeks Remain in the continental United States during the programme Attend the assigned location in person under Capital One’s hybrid model Possess valid employment authorisation that does not require employer immigration support Work Authorisation and Sponsorship Capital One states that it will not sponsor new applicants for employment authorisation or provide immigration-related support for either internship. The company specifically states that it will not support work-authorisation categories including: H-1B F-1 Optional Practical Training F-1 STEM Optional Practical Training F-1 Curricular Practical Training J-1 TN E-3 O-1 Other employer-supported immigration categories Applicants must therefore already possess independent authorisation that allows them to participate without immigration assistance from Capital One. International students who would need Curricular Practical Training, Optional Practical Training or employer support are not eligible under the stated conditions. Work Arrangement Neither programme is fully remote. Interns must be: Located in the continental United States Available for in-person work Able to attend their assigned Capital One office Prepared to follow the company’s hybrid working model Applicants should consider relocation, housing, transport and commuting requirements before applying. The internship descriptions do not state whether relocation or housing assistance will be provided. Internship Benefits Capital One states that it offers a comprehensive set of health, financial and other benefits. Eligibility can vary according to employment status, classification and other programme conditions. Candidates should consult the official listing and offer documents to determine which benefits apply to summer interns. Beyond compensation, the programmes offer professional benefits such as: Hands-on technical experience Access to internal training Mentorship Exposure to senior leaders Networking opportunities Volunteer activities Experience working in large technical organisations Consideration for future full-time rotational programmes Application Timeline and Deadline The listings do not provide a fixed final application date. Capital One states that each role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of five business days. Because internship applications can attract very high interest, the postings may not remain open for long. Candidates should apply immediately rather than assuming that the vacancies will remain available throughout August. The Technology Internship Program listing was posted on 3 August 2026 . Applicants should check the official careers pages to confirm whether each programme remains open. Application Preparation Tips Prepare Academic Documentation Technology Internship Program applicants may be asked to provide: An unofficial transcript A degree audit Another formal school record The document must confirm the applicant’s expected graduation date. Cyber applicants should also ensure their application accurately reflects their current programme and expected graduation date. Tailor the Résumé Candidates should tailor their résumé to the selected programme. Technology applicants may highlight: Software projects Programming languages Cloud experience Web or mobile development Artificial intelligence tools Hackathons Open-source contributions Technical internships Engineering coursework Cyber applicants may highlight: Security projects Capture-the-flag competitions Home laboratories Network analysis Digital forensics Incident response Security certifications Relevant coursework Programming projects Cybersecurity clubs Demonstrate Practical Experience Applicants should explain what they built, investigated or improved. A strong technical résumé should describe: The problem addressed The tools used The applicant’s individual contribution The result or impact Any measurable improvement Explain Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools Both programmes identify experience with interactive artificial intelligence tooling as a preferred qualification. Applicants may describe how they used AI tools to: Accelerate development Debug code Generate tests Review security findings Explore technical documentation Improve code quality Automate repetitive tasks They should also demonstrate that they understand how to verify AI-generated outputs rather than accepting them blindly. Artificial intelligence is a useful co-pilot, but it should not be allowed to fly the aircraft while everyone else naps. Equal Opportunity and Accommodation Capital One identifies itself as an equal opportunity employer and states that it complies with applicable federal, state and local non-discrimination laws. Qualified applicants will be considered without unlawful discrimination, including individuals with disabilities and veterans. Applicants who need reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process may contact: Telephone: 1-800-304-9102 Email: RecruitingAccommodation@capitalone.com Information provided in an accommodation request will be kept confidential and used only as necessary to provide support. For technical questions about the recruitment process, applicants may contact: Careers@capitalone.com Conclusion The Capital One Summer 2027 internships provide two distinct pathways for students interested in building careers in technology. The Technology Internship Program offers experience in software engineering, cloud platforms, full-stack development, artificial intelligence-assisted development and large-scale digital products. The Cyber Security Internship Program offers exposure to network defence, security engineering, cloud and application security, cyber risk, vulnerability assessment and incident response. Both programmes are full-time, paid ten-week internships running from June through August 2027. Participants must work from an assigned Capital One location under the company’s hybrid working model and continue in the same full-time degree programme after the internship. Capital One will not provide employment sponsorship or immigration-related support. Applicants must therefore have independent authorisation to work in the United States. Because the programmes may receive a large volume of applications and are guaranteed to remain open for only a minimum of five business days, eligible candidates should apply as soon as possible. title: AAUW International Fellowships 2027–2028 for Women in STEM: Fully Funded Graduate Study Opportunity for International Women
summary: The AAUW International Fellowships is one of the world s longest-running and most prestigious funding programs dedicated to advancing women s education and leadership. Established in 1917 , this fellowship has empowered thousands of outstanding women from around the world to pursue graduate education while developing the expertise, leadership skills, and professional experience needed to create meaningful change in their home countries and communities. The program is designed specifically for women who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents and who intend to pursue full-time postgraduate studies in the United States in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) disciplines. In addition, AAUW also offers a limited number of fellowships for women pursuing graduate study in countries other than their own. By investing in talented women scholars, researchers, innovators, and future leaders, AAUW seeks to promote educational equity, gender equality, and sustainable global development. About the AAUW International Fellowships The American Association of University Women (AAUW) created the International Fellowships program to remove financial barriers that prevent talented women from pursuing advanced education. For more than a century, the fellowship has supported international women committed to academic excellence and leadership. Fellows are expected not only to excel academically but also to use the knowledge and experience gained through their education to improve the lives of others, particularly women and girls, after completing their studies. The fellowship reflects AAUW s mission of advancing equity for women through education, research, advocacy, and leadership development. Purpose of the Fellowship The AAUW International Fellowships aim to: Promote educational opportunities for women worldwide. Support international women pursuing graduate education. Increase women s participation in STEM disciplines. Develop future women leaders. Encourage graduates to apply their expertise to benefit their home countries and communities. Strengthen global leadership among women scholars and professionals. Empower women to mentor and support future generations of girls and women. Fields of Study The fellowship primarily supports graduate programs in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) disciplines. Eligible fields include, but are not limited to: Science Technology Engineering Mathematics Medicine Applicants whose academic programs are not explicitly listed may verify whether their degree qualifies by consulting the DHS STEM Designated Degree Program List , which AAUW uses to determine STEM eligibility. Degree Levels Supported AAUW International Fellowships support women pursuing: Master s degree programs Academic doctoral degree programs Professional doctoral degree programs The fellowship supports full-time postgraduate study. Limited Awards Outside the United States While the majority of awards support graduate study in the United States, AAUW also provides a limited number of fellowships for women studying in countries other than their own . This provides additional opportunities for exceptional applicants whose educational goals are better served through graduate education outside both the United States and their home country. Who Should Apply? AAUW seeks applicants who demonstrate: Outstanding academic achievement. Strong leadership potential. Commitment to advancing women and girls. A desire to use their education to improve their communities. Dedication to creating positive social impact through their careers. APPLY HERE Applicants are expected to possess a clear vision of how their graduate education will contribute to development and progress within their home countries or communities. Eligibility Requirements To be considered for the AAUW International Fellowships, applicants must: Be women. Be non-U.S. citizens or non-permanent residents of the United States. Apply for full-time graduate study. Pursue eligible master s or doctoral programs. Study within eligible STEM disciplines. Demonstrate academic excellence. Show commitment to empowering women and girls. Intend to apply the knowledge, leadership, and professional skills gained through their studies in service to their home countries or communities after completing their education. title: Science for Africa Foundation Event Scholarships 2027: Apply for Funding to Attend the Global Mental Health in Africa Conference (GMHAC2027)
summary: The Science for Africa Foundation, in partnership with the Mental Health Innovation Network, is offering a limited number of Event Scholarships to support individuals who want to participate in the Global Mental Health in Africa Conference 2027 (#GMHAC2027) but face financial barriers. The scholarship initiative is designed to ensure that the voices shaping the future of mental health across Africa are represented at one of the continent s leading mental health gatherings. Recognizing that financial constraints often prevent talented researchers, students, practitioners, advocates, and individuals with lived experience from attending international conferences, this scholarship seeks to remove those barriers and promote greater inclusion. If you are passionate about advancing mental health research, policy, services, or advocacy across Africa, this opportunity could enable you to attend the conference while receiving financial support for key participation expenses. About the Science for Africa Foundation Event Scholarships The Science for Africa Foundation and the Mental Health Innovation Network believe that meaningful conversations about mental health in Africa should include the people who are directly involved in improving mental health systems and services across the continent. Through these scholarships, selected participants will receive financial support that enables them to attend #GMHAC2027 and contribute to discussions on research, innovation, policy, practice, and lived experiences in mental health. The scholarships are highly competitive, with only a limited number of awards available. Why These Scholarships Matter Mental health continues to be one of the most important public health priorities across Africa. However, many talented professionals and advocates are unable to attend major conferences due to financial limitations. These scholarships aim to: Increase African participation in global mental health discussions Support early-career professionals developing careers in mental health Amplify the voices of people with lived experience Encourage collaboration among researchers, practitioners, policymakers, students, and advocates Promote stronger community engagement in mental health initiatives Build networks that strengthen mental health systems across Africa Who Can Apply? The scholarship is open to individuals working in or connected to mental health across Africa. Eligible applicants include: 1. Early-Career Researchers Researchers involved in: Mental health research Public health research Clinical research Mental health policy Mental health practice 2. Students Students are eligible to apply provided they submit: A letter of support from their institution, supervisor, or academic advisor 3. Persons with Lived Experience Individuals with: Personal lived experience of mental health conditions Psychosocial disabilities Experience contributing to advocacy or community engagement 4. Other Mental Health Professionals Applicants who have a demonstrated connection to mental health in Africa may also apply. Examples include individuals working in: Mental health advocacy Community organizations NGOs Healthcare delivery Government agencies Social work Psychology Psychiatry Public health Policy development Applicants should clearly explain their role in the application. Priority for African-Based Applicants While several categories of applicants are eligible, priority will be given to: Applicants based in Africa Individuals whose attendance depends on financial assistance Applicants making meaningful contributions to mental health across the continent What the Scholarship Can Cover Applicants may request financial support for one or more of the following expenses: Conference Registration Support for: Conference participation fees Travel Costs Funding for transportation to and from the conference venue. Accommodation Support for lodging during the conference period. Other Costs Applicants may also request support for additional conference-related expenses by explaining their needs within the application. Required Application Materials Applications are submitted online and require several documents and written responses. Personal Information Applicants must provide: Full name Email address Telephone number Country of residence Institution or organization Current professional role Motivation Statement Applicants must prepare a statement of no more than 300 words explaining: Why they wish to attend #GMHAC2027 How participation will benefit their work What they hope to gain from the conference Impact and Contribution Statement Applicants should explain: How their work contributes to improving mental health in Africa Their impact on research, services, policy, or advocacy How they involve people with lived experience or community engagement in their work Financial Need Statement Applicants must submit a statement (maximum 300 words) describing: Why financial support is necessary Why they would otherwise be unable to attend Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Résumé Applicants must upload an up-to-date CV or résumé. Recommendation Letter Mandatory for student applicants Strongly encouraged for all other applicants Selection Process The scholarships are competitive and limited. Applications will be reviewed based on: Eligibility Demonstrated impact in mental health Quality of motivation statement Financial need Potential contribution to the conference Overall strength of the application Meeting the eligibility criteria alone does not guarantee funding. Notification of Results All applicants will receive notification of the outcome of their application via email. Successful applicants will receive additional information regarding: Scholarship coverage Participation requirements Next steps before the conference Click HERE to read more. Scholarship Terms and Conditions Applicants should carefully review the scholarship conditions before applying. Important conditions include: Scholarships are limited in number. Awards are competitive. Meeting eligibility requirements does not guarantee selection. Applications must contain accurate and complete information. Scholarships cannot be transferred to another individual. Tips for Preparing a Strong Application To improve your application: Clearly explain your connection to mental health in Africa. Demonstrate the impact of your work using concrete examples. Show how attending the conference will strengthen your research, practice, advocacy, or policy work. Be honest and specific when explaining financial need. Submit a well-organized CV. Obtain a strong recommendation letter, especially if you are a student. Review all documents carefully before submission. APPLY HERE Benefits of the Event Scholarship Successful applicants may receive support for: Conference registration fees Travel expenses Accommodation costs Other approved participation expenses Access to one of Africa s leading mental health conferences Networking opportunities with researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and advocates Opportunities to collaborate with experts and organizations working to strengthen mental health across Africa Exposure to innovative research, policies, and best practices in mental health Conclusion The Science for Africa Foundation Event Scholarships provide an important opportunity for individuals working to improve mental health across Africa to participate in the Global Mental Health in Africa Conference 2027. By reducing financial barriers, the program ensures that researchers, students, practitioners, policymakers, advocates, and people with lived experience can contribute to meaningful conversations that shape the future of mental health on the continent. If you are committed to advancing mental health research, services, policy, or advocacy in Africa and require financial assistance to attend #GMHAC2027, this scholarship offers an excellent opportunity to gain new knowledge, build professional networks, and contribute your voice to one of Africa s most important mental health events. Be sure to prepare a compelling application with strong supporting documents to maximize your chances of selection. Click HERE for more scholarship opportunities. title: FoodHaus Fellowship for Action 2026–2027: Nine-Month Food Systems Leadership Programme
summary: Applications remain open for the second cohort of the FoodHaus Fellowship for Action 2026–2027 , a nine-month learning programme for people who want to contribute to a more regenerative, equitable and sustainable food future. The fellowship supports participants in moving from an initial question or idea toward a concrete food-systems project or intervention. It combines systems thinking, leadership development, personal reflection, practical experimentation, peer learning and individual coaching. Participants do not need to come from a traditional food-sector background. The programme welcomes people from different professions, communities, cultures and areas of expertise who share an interest in transforming the way food is grown, distributed, accessed and experienced. The programme will begin online on 12 October 2026 and conclude at the end of August 2027 . It includes two intensive in-person weeks in Switzerland, supported by a longer period of online learning, coaching and project development. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the programme is full, with a final application deadline of 31 August 2026 . All scholarships have already been allocated, so FoodHaus is currently accepting paid applications only. Online Information Session Prospective applicants who would like to understand the programme before applying can attend an online information session on: 24 August 2026, from 4:30 to 5:30 p.m. CEST The session will introduce the FoodHaus Fellowship for Action, explain its learning model and provide more information about the in-person immersion weeks in Switzerland. Participants will also be able to meet members of the FoodHaus team and ask questions live. To register for the information session, CLICK HERE . Application Deadline The final application deadline is: 31 August 2026 Applications are considered on a rolling basis and may close earlier if the cohort becomes full. Interested candidates are therefore encouraged to apply as soon as they are ready rather than waiting until the final day. The earlier scholarship and early-bird deadline of 1 July 2026 has passed. All available scholarships have already been awarded, and only paid applications are currently being accepted. About the FoodHaus Fellowship for Action The FoodHaus Fellowship for Action is designed for people who want to create meaningful change in how food is produced, shared and experienced. Over nine months, participants will explore a food-related question, initiative or area of concern and develop it into a more concrete intervention. Along the way, they will build practical skills for working with complexity, collaborating with others and leading change within their organisations, communities or professional fields. The programme combines personal development with practical action. Its purpose is not simply to teach participants about food systems but to help them clarify where they can contribute and begin turning that contribution into something tangible. The fellowship may be particularly relevant to people who: Want to deepen their understanding of food systems and move toward action Have an early-stage project, idea or question they want to develop Want greater clarity about their role in food-systems transformation Value inner development and relationship-building alongside technical tools Want to collaborate with an international community Are ready to involve their organisation, community or local network in creating change Programme Duration The fellowship will run from: 12 October 2026 to the end of August 2027 The programme includes three connected phases: An opening online phase and an intensive week in Switzerland A longer period of online learning, coaching and project development A final in-person week in Switzerland for reflection, presentation and celebration The first intensive week will take place from: 25–31 October 2026 The concluding intensive week will take place from: 8–14 August 2027 Weekly online sessions are scheduled from 3:00 to 4:00 p.m. CET or CEST , depending on the time of year. What Fellows Will Experience 1. Food Systems Learning Participants will learn to understand food as a complex and interconnected system. The fellowship introduces systems-thinking approaches that help participants examine relationships among agriculture, markets, culture, health, climate, policy, power, communities and the environment. Fellows will explore how different stakeholders influence food systems and how narratives, power relations and institutional structures can either support or obstruct change. They will also examine innovative initiatives, networks and people already working to create more regenerative and equitable food futures. The objective is not to present one universal solution. Food systems are tangled forests, not flat-pack furniture. Participants will instead build a toolkit for navigating complexity and identifying possible leverage points for action. 2. Development of a Concrete Initiative The fellowship supports participants in clarifying and developing a project, intervention or contribution. Fellows will examine: The issue they want to address The communities or stakeholders involved The purpose of their proposed intervention The assumptions behind their idea Possible strategies for implementation Resources and relationships required Risks, uncertainties and barriers The type of impact they hope to create Participants will be guided through a facilitated development process intended to help an initiative move from “soil to seedling.” They will also build a customised toolkit that can support implementation after the programme. The fellowship is suitable for someone beginning with a broad question as well as someone who already has an initiative but feels stuck, overwhelmed or uncertain about the next step. 3. Leadership and Personal Development FoodHaus places personal and relational development at the centre of the fellowship. Participants will examine how their values, habits, relationships and leadership practices affect their ability to contribute to change. The programme aims to help fellows: Move from overwhelm toward grounded action Build greater self-awareness Develop more sustainable leadership practices Strengthen collaboration and communication Create spaces for collective reflection and action Relate more effectively to themselves, other people and the wider world Fellows will learn practical skills for building community and facilitating spaces in which change can emerge. 4. Weekly Online Learning Following the first immersion week, fellows will continue through an online learning experience that includes regular sessions, weekly experiments, community calls and peer support. The online component allows participants to remain active in their professional, organisational or community contexts while testing ideas and applying what they learn. Weekly activities may involve: Systems-thinking exercises Reflection tasks Project-development experiments Peer conversations Expert contributions Community learning sessions Practical leadership exercises Preparation for local action Participants are expected to take an active role in shaping their own learning rather than remaining passive recipients of course material. 5. Personal Coaching and Mentorship Participants receive personalised leadership and development coaching from FoodHaus’s pool of integral coaches. Coaching sessions help fellows design their own development journeys and explore questions related to purpose, leadership, relationships, uncertainty and project implementation. Participants are also supported by the programme team and facilitators throughout the fellowship. This personal support may help fellows: Clarify their goals Recognise recurring challenges Develop greater confidence Maintain momentum Work through uncertainty Strengthen their leadership approach Connect personal development with practical action 6. International Peer Learning Fellows become part of a diverse international community of changemakers. Participants learn through regular exchanges, group sessions, coaching activities and in-person intensives. The programme is designed to create a trusting environment in which people can discuss challenges, test ideas, share experiences and support one another. This international community may bring together people working in different parts of food systems and in different cultural or professional contexts. The diversity of the cohort is intended to expose participants to new assumptions, approaches and ways of understanding change. 7. Two In-Person Intensive Weeks in Switzerland The programme begins and ends with an in-person immersion week in Switzerland. Both intensive weeks are held at Gut Rheinau , a biodynamic farm and learning centre. The experience includes living, learning and working together in a shared environment. During the first intensive week, participants will: Meet other fellows and the programme team Begin designing their learning journeys Explore food-systems complexity Reflect on their personal contribution Build trust within the cohort Begin shaping their initiatives The programme also includes excursions to meet food initiatives and changemakers. The second intensive week provides an opportunity to: Reflect on the nine-month learning journey Share lessons and project progress Present developing initiatives Consolidate tools for future action Celebrate the cohort’s work Prepare for continued implementation after the fellowship Who Should Apply? The fellowship is open to individuals aged 21 or older who have a demonstrated interest in food-related challenges and creating change. Applicants may come from any educational or professional background, although some working experience is expected. Participants should be comfortable communicating in English, documenting their work and using online platforms. They must also have reliable internet access and be available for both intensive weeks in Switzerland. The programme may suit applicants who: Have the beginning of an idea and want to shape it into action Work within a food-related organisation and want to create change from within Belong to a community that could benefit from a new initiative Want to support an existing food-systems innovation Feel overwhelmed by the complexity of their project Are moving through a professional transition Want to work with a colleague or co-creator on a shared initiative Applicants do not need to arrive with a completed proposal. The fellowship is designed to support people moving from an initial question or emerging idea toward a practical contribution. Benefits of the FoodHaus Fellowship for Action Leadership Development Participants will strengthen their ability to lead collaboratively and act in complex environments. They will explore how to create change without relying solely on authority, technical expertise or rigid plans. Food Systems Understanding Fellows will learn to examine food systems from multiple perspectives and identify relationships among stakeholders, policies, markets, communities and ecosystems. Project Development Participants will receive guidance in designing and testing a food-related initiative. The fellowship provides a structured process for translating an idea into practical steps while recognising that meaningful change rarely follows a neat, obedient line. International Community Fellows will build relationships with participants from different sectors, cultures and regions. These connections may lead to future collaboration, peer support and shared learning beyond the formal programme. Personal Growth Participants will strengthen self-awareness, resilience, relational skills and confidence. The programme treats inner development as part of systems change rather than as a decorative wellness break placed between technical sessions. Coaching and Mentoring Each fellow receives access to individual coaching and continuing support from programme facilitators. Immersive Learning in Switzerland The two residential weeks offer an opportunity to connect food-systems concepts with practical experience in a biodynamic farm setting. Diverse Backgrounds Welcome FoodHaus encourages applications from people with varied professional and lived experiences. Potential participants may include: Farmers Chefs Social entrepreneurs Policymakers Scientists Educators Artists and creatives Activists Community organisers Administrators Social workers Development professionals Nonprofit practitioners Public-sector professionals People in professional transition FoodHaus expects the cohort to include people from many more backgrounds beyond these examples. Programme Fees and Scholarship Update The standard programme fees are: Swiss applicants: CHF 3,400 International applicants: CHF 2,900 Participants are also responsible for their own travel costs for the two intensive weeks in Switzerland. The difference between the Swiss and international fees reflects these additional travel considerations. The scholarship deadline has passed, and all scholarships have already been allocated. FoodHaus is therefore currently accepting paid applications only . Applicants should review the official programme information carefully to understand what is included in the fee and what additional costs they will need to cover. Application Process Applicants must complete the official FoodHaus application form. They should be prepared to upload: A one-page CV in PDF format A personal story A voice note or video Applicants who plan to participate as part of a community or organisation are encouraged to join with one or more co-creators. Each participant must submit an individual application, but applicants can identify their co-creators in the relevant section of the form. Participating with colleagues may make it easier to develop and implement a shared local initiative. APPLY HERE Why This Fellowship Matters Food systems shape health, livelihoods, climate resilience, biodiversity, culture, land use and social relationships. Transforming them requires more than isolated technical solutions. It requires people who can understand complexity, build relationships, work across sectors and continue acting even when the path ahead looks like a plate of spaghetti designed by a committee. The FoodHaus Fellowship for Action supports participants in combining analysis with action and personal development with collective change. It recognises that lasting food-systems transformation depends not only on what people do but also on how they lead, listen, collaborate and sustain themselves. Final Thoughts The FoodHaus Fellowship for Action 2026–2027 offers a structured nine-month journey for people ready to develop a meaningful contribution to food-systems transformation. Through systems thinking, leadership development, personal coaching, peer learning and two in-person immersion weeks in Switzerland, participants will gain the support and practical tools needed to move from intention toward action. The programme begins on 12 October 2026 , and applications will be accepted until the cohort is full or no later than 31 August 2026 . Prospective applicants can attend the online information session on 24 August 2026 from 4:30 to 5:30 p.m. CEST to meet the FoodHaus team and ask questions. All scholarships have been allocated, and only paid applications are currently available. To learn more about the programme and apply, CLICK HERE .
